sharedGuidance: Use existing feature/page/service and isolated browser → API → PostgreSQL test seams. Each slice owns its meaningful regression tests and runs required owning-project checks plus the repository-required isolated end-to-end suite before completion. Preserve accepted Rule-storage/reconciliation ADRs, frontend feature boundaries, existing authorization and atomic import behavior; validate both sides of any discovered API contract adjustment. No new test framework, Review editing, numerical forecasts, automatic Budget changes, or private financial fixtures.

tickets.title: Show correct Space identity and discoverable Budget navigation
tickets.deliverable: Users see Personal consistently throughout the application and Statement Import, and can find Budgets while retaining the four mobile tabs.
criteria: Resolve labels from actual Space identity/kind: an explicit Personal Space ID never displays Shared; the shell and all import stages show the correct Space.
Retain the import destination lock when a file is accepted; labels and later commit destination remain consistent.
Keep Dashboard, Imports, Transactions, and Insights as the four mobile tabs; rename the Categories menu destination to Budgets and retain Category management and existing route compatibility.
Provide Manage Budgets from Dashboard and Monthly Insights without changing the selected Space or Reporting Period.
Verify explicit-ID Personal routes on phone and desktop, existing authorization/cache isolation, accessible navigation, and updated design-system guidance.

tickets.title: Make monthly Budget status and Dashboard summaries consistent
tickets.deliverable: Dashboard distinguishes total, Budgeted, and Unbudgeted Spending and exposes Category risks even when aggregate usage is low; all existing Budget presentations use exact status boundaries.
criteria: Use exact cents: below 80% Within Budget; 80% to below 100% Nearing Budget; exactly 100% At Budget Limit; above 100% Over Budget. Round display values only.
Apply the policy consistently to Dashboard, existing Insights/Category summaries, and available chart details through a narrowly shared policy for concrete callers.
Label the aggregate Budgeted spending / total monthly limits, using only monthly-budgeted Categories in its numerator and current monthly limits in its denominator.
Show total recorded spending and Unbudgeted Spending separately; yearly-only Categories and Uncategorized contribute to Unbudgeted Spending.
Show individual Category status and exact remaining/over amounts despite low aggregate usage. When there are no monthly limits, show setup guidance rather than an invalid percentage.

Test PHP 799.99, 800.00, 999.99, 1000.00, and 1000.01 against a PHP 1000 limit, display rounding traps, yearly-only/no Budgets, and a breach hidden by low aggregate usage. Do not claim empty recorded months are complete or healthy.

tickets.title: Make filtered Transaction counts and totals match the result
tickets.deliverable: Users filtering Transactions see the complete filtered count and expense total, with clearly secondary whole-month context.
criteria: Show the total count and expense amount for the complete filtered result across pagination, not the current page or an unfiltered month.
Any whole-month count or amount is explicitly labeled and secondary; filters and summaries visibly agree.
Category, date, search, and account filters update both result and summary; clearing filters restores normal monthly results.
Reset pagination and isolate cache identity when filter or Space scope changes; avoid showing a stale summary under a new filter.

Use existing query/API boundaries; inspect available summary capabilities and paginate/aggregate correctly if needed, rather than assuming the first page is the complete result. Any contract adjustment is validated on API and browser sides.
Verify multiple pages, combined filters, empty results, failure/retry, and preservation of Reporting Period and Space.

tickets.title: Open newly imported Transactions across every statement month
tickets.deliverable: After a confirmed import, Users see a focused success message and can browse precisely the saved statement expenses across months before returning to their previous monthly view.
criteria: Success scrolls to and focuses the announced confirmation heading and shows the destination Space, included expense count, and total.
View Transactions passes the destination Space and Committed Statement Import identity; use the existing API statementImportId filter and bypass the browser month clamp in statement scope.
Show a visible statement filter/context, recorded expense activity date range, complete filtered count, and total. Do not describe the activity range as complete coverage.
Replace the month picker during statement scope; additional filters narrow that scope without including unrelated expenses.
Return to monthly view restores the prior Reporting Period; scope changes reset pagination/cache context and provide honest loading/error/empty states.

Test a fictional committed statement spanning two months, unrelated same-date expenses, a prior Reporting Period outside that range, extra filters, pagination, and Space ownership. Reconciliation, duplicate protection, and atomic commit remain unchanged.

tickets.title: Make individual mobile categorization fast and explicit
tickets.deliverable: Users assign Categories in a compact phone interaction, retain full corrections, and explicitly advance through included Unmapped Transactions.
criteria: Provide compact Category assignment while preserving full description, date, amount, and Category corrections in Categorize.
Do not apply an assignment merely on Category selection; Apply & next explicitly saves and advances to the next included Unmapped row in the selected order using stable row identities.
When no included Unmapped row remains, show completion feedback and the normal route to Review; do not automatically commit.
Eligible expense exclusion/re-inclusion remains reversible in Categorize and updates summaries; ineligible payment/credit activity remains ineligible.
Failures retain entered values and editor position; selected order and filters remain usable across repeated assignments.

Verify 320px/390px phones, desktop, keyboard/focus behavior, full corrections, exclusion/re-inclusion, next-row skipping, and coexistence with existing Category Suggestions. Avoid changing Rule semantics in this slice.

tickets.title: Apply Categories to repeated statement descriptions with preview
tickets.deliverable: Users categorize repeated descriptions in one statement through a controlled preview without overwriting previously reviewed work.
criteria: Default candidates to included Unmapped expense rows with the same normalized full description in the current Statement Import.
Normalize case and whitespace using existing matching semantics; retain punctuation and do not infer merchant identity or search other imports.
Preview the affected rows and count, permit deselection, and apply one Category only to the selected rows.
Preserve existing assignments unless explicitly selected for replacement; default selection never changes or re-includes excluded rows.
Bulk assignment is Manual and temporary; it never implicitly creates a persistent Category Rule or rewrites reviewed assignments.
Test normalized repeats, punctuation distinctions, deselection, explicit replacement, excluded rows, empty selection, and consistent summaries through Review and commit.

tickets.title: Encourage Remember with safe Rule saves and clear recovery
tickets.deliverable: Users understand Remember's future benefit, opt into a predictable Exact Rule, and recover from failure or conflict without losing their draft.
criteria: Remember remains unchecked but prominent wherever useful, explains future-import benefits, and suppresses redundant encouragement for an equivalent Rule.

Default to Exact; offer Contains explicitly with substring semantics and current-statement match preview. Preserve Exact precedence, normalized matching, inactive-Category restrictions, and reviewed assignments.
Apply & remember persists the Rule immediately before the local assignment and confirms Rule saved for future imports; it is separate from atomic import confirmation.
Rule failure/conflict applies no local assignment and retains all editor inputs; offer Retry and Apply without remembering.
A conflicting normalized pattern/match type names the existing Category and is never silently replaced. Equivalent same-Category Rules are reused without duplicates.
Leaving/discarding explains that draft Transactions are discarded but saved Rules remain. Handle uncertain network completion honestly and retry through equivalent-Rule reuse.

Verify failure/retry, conflict, equivalence, immediate persistence before confirmation, draft discard, current suggestions/bulk coexistence, and Space-scoped authorization. Do not introduce distributed transaction semantics.

tickets.title: Keep Review read-only and preserve correction context
tickets.deliverable: Users inspect every parsed statement row with clear expense/exclusion language and return to Categorize for corrections without losing their place.
criteria: Review contains no editing controls; one Back to Categorize action restores the previous sort, filters, and position.
Show included expenses first in the chosen order and an expandable excluded section with reasons. Previous Categorize filters never silently hide Review rows.
Keep a sticky included expense count and total reachable without obscuring rows, confirmation, or mobile navigation.
Present expenses with positive readable amounts rather than green Credit based on internal parser sign; identify payments and other credits accurately using provider-supported information.
Keep expense-only persistence and existing eligibility: payments/other credits remain excluded; eligible expenses can be re-included in Categorize.

Preserve reconciliation, duplicate warnings, explicit confirmation, and atomic commit. Test hidden-by-filter rows, ordering within groups, exclusion reasons, Back restoration, and no-edit behavior across mobile/desktop.
Preserve newer categorization/Remember functionality as it lands; this ticket does not need to wait for bulk assignment or Remember redesign to deliver read-only Review.

tickets.title: Lead Monthly Insights with actionable Category risks
tickets.deliverable: Users immediately see selected-month risks and can investigate Transactions or edit/set a Category Budget while preserving context.
criteria: Place the selected Reporting Period, recorded spending summary, and Category attention states before historical totals/charts.
Surface individual Nearing Budget, At Budget Limit, and Over Budget states; do not present a breach in a low-spending ranking without its warning.
Provide View Transactions and Edit Budget/Set Budget actions carrying Space, month, and Category; return/cancel restores the originating view and filters.
Budgeted, total, and Unbudgeted summaries use the agreed scope and exact status policy; no-budget and empty states provide useful actions without completeness claims.
For the current month, show actual usage alongside elapsed-month progress labeled as recorded spending. Historical periods show actual historical spending; do not add numerical forecasts.

Verify contextual handoffs, filtered totals, return/cancel, changed Reporting Period, mobile hierarchy, desktop consistency, and accessibility. Statement-scoped browsing is not a prerequisite for month-scoped actions.

tickets.title: Explain potential unusual Category spending using recorded history
tickets.deliverable: Users see conservative potential-spending-pattern signals with transparent comparison evidence and contributing Transactions, or an honest insufficient-history state.
criteria: Use up to six preceding calendar months and require at least three positive recorded Category comparisons; do not reach further back to fill missing months.

For the current month compare through the equivalent day, clamping shorter months; for a historical selected month use full months. Exclude comparisons with no recorded Category spending and prevent selected/future month leakage.
Flag only when the selected amount is at least 1.5 times the median AND at least PHP 500 above it; use exact amounts, including precision for even-sized medians.
Show selected amount, baseline window/cutoff, contributing months, median, relative/absolute change, and contributing Transactions with useful investigation actions.

Show insufficient recorded history below three eligible comparisons and describe potential patterns in recorded spending; no-signal and empty data are not proof of normal spending or complete coverage.

Test eligibility/window boundaries, both noise thresholds and equality, even medians, partial months, shorter months/leap years, future leakage, sparse data, and visible explanation/actions. Do not add affordability judgments or forecasts.

tickets.title: Suggest Budget review from recurring breaches and disclose historical effects
tickets.deliverable: Users can assess recurring Category breaches, review a current recurring Budget, and understand that changing it affects historical comparisons.
criteria: Suggest reviewing a monthly Budget after breaches in at least three of the last six eligible recorded Category months.

Use completed months at/before a historical selected period or before the current partial month; exclude future periods and months without recorded Category spending. Show actual eligible denominator and current-limit evidence.
Open the Category's existing Budget editor with evidence available; Unbudgeted Categories offer Set Budget. The User enters and explicitly saves any new amount; never auto-adjust limits.
Before saving, explain historical comparisons will use the new current recurring limit; label historical views accordingly and refresh dependent queries after success.
Preserve yearly Budgets, current positive monthly limits, existing stale-write protection, Space authorization, and cancellation/return context; add no effective-dated Budget history.

Test recurring breach eligibility/counts, exact-limit non-breach, historical/current cutoffs, no-monthly-Budget actions, save/cancel/stale failure, and recalculated historical evidence. This slice is independent of unusual-spending median signals.

tickets.title: Make chart selection and spending inspection usable on phones
tickets.deliverable: Users inspect monthly trends and daily spikes through readable touch/keyboard details and a compact Category selector without silently changing their Reporting Period.
criteria: Default comparisons to the three highest-spending available Categories for the chart range, or all if fewer; provide a compact selector for changing/adding Categories.
Keep stable Category Colors across views and distinguish Categories that share a color through labels/other cues; use readable month/year labels.
Touch, pointer, and keyboard inspection opens equivalent details with date/month, totals, Category breakdown, Budget states, contributing Transactions, and contextual actions.
Inspection alone preserves Reporting Period; only explicit View this month changes it. Subsequent Transaction actions carry inspected context and dismissal restores focus.
Preserve accessible tables and nonvisual detail access; aria-hidden charts must not be the sole interactive path, and overlays/tab bars leave controls reachable.
Explain recorded daily-spike contributions even without enough historical data for a potential-pattern signal; chart inspection does not depend on that signal engine.
Verify default/fewer Categories, selector updates, duplicate colors, keyboard/touch interaction, month navigation, focus, readable phone layouts, desktop behavior, and light/dark tokens.

tickets.title: Verify the complete mobile spending-monitoring journey
tickets.deliverable: A deterministic isolated browser/API/PostgreSQL journey proves the full redesigned experience works consistently from Dashboard through import and spending actions.
criteria: Use fictional reconciled and encrypted PDF fixtures spanning two months through real Upload/parsing; never publish the User's statement, password, identifiers, or private evidence.

Exercise Personal Dashboard → unlock → individual/bulk assignment and Remember → exclusion/re-inclusion → read-only Review → confirmation → statement-scoped Transactions → monthly return → Monthly Insights → Transactions/Budget action → return.

Assert persisted destination, expense count/amount, saved Rule behavior, exact Budget states, explicit filtered/statement scope, and preserved Reporting Period/context; protect atomic rollback and duplicate confirmation behavior.

Exercise 320px and 390px phone layouts and 1440px desktop, reachable sticky controls/tab bars, no horizontal page overflow, keyboard details, focus/success announcements, accessible tables, stable colors, and light/dark semantic tokens.
Resolve cross-feature regressions exposed by this journey and reconcile implemented design-system/visual-reference guidance; preserve Category Suggestions and unrelated work.

Run owning-project checks and the required isolated browser/API/PostgreSQL suite; report actual validation results. This final journey complements rather than postpones each earlier ticket's own acceptance tests.
